title: What Space Food Systems 2.0 Is
definition: Space Food Systems 2.0: next-gen food for deep-space crews.
description:
Space Food Systems 2.0: next-gen food for deep-space crews. This is Future Food Systems at its most ambitious — shelf-stable meals research, system logistics engineering and mass budgets operations converging on a single goal: making system hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Food Systems will decide crew morale outcomes this century. Space Food Systems 2.0 is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working system hulls, the larger shelf-stable meals vision stalls, and with it, the system logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Space Food Systems 2.0 in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

title: Real Research Today: Space Food Systems 2.0
definition: Today's documented research behind Space Food Systems 2.0.
description:
The road to Space Food Systems 2.0 is already being paved. Vertical farming (AeroFarms, Plenty) grows leafy greens with 95% less water. The UN Decade of Family Farming recognizes smallholders feeding a third of humanity.

The EAT-Lancet Commission defined the planetary health diet for people and Earth. Together these programs form the shelf-stable meals foundation that Space Food Systems 2.0 will build on — the system logistics results, the mass budgets methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as system logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First system hulls products reach price parity: shelf-stable mea

description:

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed shelf-stable meals demonstrations, system logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting mass budgets uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Space Food Systems 2.0
definition: Estimates Space Food Systems 2.0 readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Space Food Systems 2.0 components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where shelf-stable meals monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or mass budgets maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Space Food Systems 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Space Food Systems 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Space Food Systems 2.0 — next-gen food for deep-space crews.

Phase 1 — Prove (shelf-stable meals): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (mass budgets): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (crew morale): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and space-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
